context.alert_text: Errors on the catalog sync function above 10 in 5 minutes

root_cause.hypothesis: The catalog-sync Lambda is failing (64 errors across 71 invocations) due to network-level failures reaching AWS service endpoints from inside its VPC: repeated DNS resolution failures and EndpointConnectionError when contacting DynamoDB (and likely RDS), not a code or deploy regression (no deploy occurred in the prior 6h).
evidence: C2 shows no deploy preceded the alert, ruling out a code/config regression as trigger
Multiple log lines show DNS and connection failures to the DynamoDB endpoint, consistent with a VPC networking/DNS issue (missing NAT or VPC endpoint, or SG blocking egress)
High error count with invocation durations reaching near the function timeout aligns with network calls hanging then failing
ruled_out: Code/deploy regression (C2: no change in prior 6h)
Memory exhaustion (F2 max_memory_used well below memory_size)

citations.quote: none on warden-dev-catalog-sync in the 6 h before the alert

proposal.reasoning: The failure pattern (DNS resolution failures and EndpointConnectionError to AWS service endpoints with no recent deploy) points to a VPC networking misconfiguration (missing/blocked VPC endpoint, NAT gateway, or security-group egress rule) rather than an application bug. None of the available automated remediation actions (restart, scale, rollback, config revert) address a network/DNS infrastructure issue, and changing security group or VPC routing is outside the safe automated action set, so a human should verify and fix the VPC/DNS/SG configuration for this Lambda.
proposal.expected_effect: A human investigates and corrects the VPC networking (DNS resolution path, NAT gateway, or security group egress rules) so the Lambda can reach DynamoDB/RDS endpoints, resolving the error spike.
